# My year ahead — planning it out

Alright, let me think this through. I've been doing this 35 years, and mostly I just keep doing what works. No big changes this year unless I have a reason.

## How I'm splitting up my 30 mu

I've got 30 mu to work. Here's how I've been doing it:

- **18 mu** for wheat-maize, that's my main land. Wheat went in last October, maize goes after wheat comes off in June.
- **7 mu** cotton on the plot near the west edge — that land is a bit sandier, cotton does fine there.
- **5 mu** garlic, went in last October same time as wheat. Garlic brings good cash, my wife and daughter-in-law help with it.

That's 30 mu total. No fallow, we need every bit producing.

## Wheat (18 mu, already planted)

The wheat is already up, now I just need to manage it through spring. I put down 2 bags of compound fertilizer (那种45%的) per mu before planting — that's the base. Now the wheat is at jointing stage, I need to topdress urea. Usually I put about 20 kg of urea per mu, maybe a little more if the field looks yellow. My neighbor 老王 last year tried skipping the second irrigation because of the water cost, and his yield was way down. So I'm not cutting corners there — I'll irrigate at jointing, again at heading, and maybe once more during grain filling if it doesn't rain.

Last year I got around 420 kg/mu, similar to the year before. I expect about the same if weather is normal.

## Maize (18 mu, plant in mid-June)

As soon as the wheat combine leaves the field, I've got maybe 5-7 days to get maize in. Time is really tight. I buy 登海 hybrid seed — been using it for years, reliable. I direct-seed right into the stubble with the small planter my cousin and I share.

Fertilizer-wise, I put the base down with the seeder — 1 bag of compound per mu. Then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage (大喇叭口期), about 25 kg urea per mu. Same as I've always done. If it's dry I irrigate once at tasseling, but if summer rain comes through I save the water money.

Last year maize was maybe 480 kg/mu. Decent.

## Cotton (7 mu, plant late April)

Cotton is more work — more bugs, more picking. Plant in late April when soil is warm. I use 中棉所 seed, buy fresh each year. Put down compound fertilizer at planting, maybe 1.5 bags per mu, and top up with urea at flowering.

Bollworm is the biggest headache. I spray probably 4-5 times through the summer — my neighbors all do the same, we kind of spray around the same time. My wife does most of the picking with help from her sister when it's heavy. We pick 3-4 times from September through October. If I can get 270 kg/mu lint I'll be happy.

## Garlic (5 mu, harvest late May)

Garlic is already growing. It went in last October. Price has been good the last couple years — last year I sold for a decent profit, so I kept the same area this year. Could be a gamble though, garlic price swings a lot.

Now through May I need to irrigate 3 more times and topdress urea twice — garlic wants a lot of water and fertilizer for good bulb size. Also spray for leaf rust once. Harvest is all hand work, family labor, maybe 20 days of intense work for all of us. Daughter-in-law usually takes time off from her factory job to help. Last year we got about 1800 kg/mu fresh.

## About the money

Seed, fertilizer, pesticide, water — all up, probably around 20,000 yuan for the year. I've got that saved from last year's harvest. Garlic cash is what usually floats me through spring.
